SMTO-EXE-0063 — SMTO's request on the Gateway computer's desktop was stopped

GUID: b377ab74-b2b8-5e8b-9ac9-9060ce260345
Slug: desktop-cancelled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • A request to work with apps or windows on the Gateway computer was stopped, either because the task was cancelled or because the same request had already been sent. An earlier copy of it may already have done the work.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the Gateway computer's screen, or ask SMTO to list the open apps and windows there, to see whether the app was already opened, closed or moved. When the same request arrives twice, SMTO blocks the second one, so the first may already have done the work.
  2. If you selected Stop on purpose, and the screen looks the way you want, you don't need to do anything else. Stopping a task cancels the desktop request that was in progress, which is what this message reports.
  3. If the action clearly did not happen and you still need it, ask SMTO for it in a new message. A new message creates a fresh request that SMTO won't mix up with the stopped one.

What success looks like

  • The app or window is in the state you wanted, and the action happened only once.

If it still fails

  • If requests keep stopping when you didn't select Stop, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a close or quit before checking the app is still open.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway Desktop service refused or interrupted the operation because its execution_id was already active or recently finished, or a cancel signal arrived during dispatch or the window wait.

What this means

  • Desktop admission found a reused active/finished execution identity, or a cancellation event interrupted dispatch or the window-wait loop. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Desktop admission found a reused active/finished execution identity, or a cancellation event interrupted dispatch or the window-wait loop.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect execution identity and cancellation state to distinguish duplicate admission from a newly requested stop.

How to fix it

  • Check whether the run was cancelled (Stop, or a /desktop/cancel call) or whether the same execution_id was resent within the Gateway's 300-second finished window. Observe current processes and windows on the same Gateway to settle the original action, then issue a new operation with a new execution_id only if it is still needed.
  • Inspect the original execution receipt and current desktop state; issue new work only if it is still needed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect any recorded execution effects before deliberately starting a new operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The original action and any effects are settled before separately authorized new desktop work.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
